entities.summary:
Miguel José de Azanza y Alegría, 1st Duke of Santa Fe, was a pivotal figure in late 18th and early 19th-century Spanish colonial and peninsular politics, serving as Viceroy of New Spain from May 31, 1798, to April 30, 1800. Born in Aoiz-Agoitz, Navarre, in 1746, Azanza's career spanned a period of profound geopolitical upheaval, marked by the decline of the Spanish Empire and the rise of Napoleonic France. His tenure in Mexico City represented a final attempt by the Bourbon monarchy to consolidate control and implement reforms in its most valuable American possession, before the continent was plunged into independence movements.

During his viceroyalty, Azanza faced the pressing challenges of maintaining stability amidst growing unrest and external threats, particularly from Great Britain. He focused on strengthening the colonial administration, improving defenses, and managing the burgeoning economy of New Spain, including addressing issues related to mining and trade. His brief but impactful administration laid groundwork for subsequent viceroys, navigating the delicate balance between royal mandates from Madrid and the complex realities of colonial governance. Prior to this, he had served in diplomatic roles, including as an envoy to Prussia, and as Minister of War in Spain, demonstrating his broad experience in both foreign policy and military administration.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Miguel José de Azanza was a significant regional figure, overseeing a crucial period of colonial administration in New Spain and later serving as a high-ranking minister in Napoleonic Spain. His choices profoundly affected his personal legacy and contributed to the political fragmentation within Spain during a period of imperial transition.
